title: Compatibility decision framework, intake metadata, and pinning guardrails for new open models
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Purpose:
This ticket formalizes a lightweight, decision-oriented framework for admitting new open-model variants into the Redwood model catalog. The goal is to reduce manual ambiguity during intake, make pinning decisions reproducible, and surface runtime compatibility notes required by the serving runtime. This is a product-facing PRD that clarifies scope (what we require at intake vs what we validate later), enumerates acceptance criteria, and prescribes a minimal metadata contract for open models so that runtime teams and catalog consumers can reason about cost/latency/regressions.
background: We continue to see ad-hoc model submissions that lack clear compatibility signals (e.g., differing kv-cache layout, quantization incompatibilities, or custom ops). Previously this generated repeated back-and-forth between PM, runtime, and model-onboarding engineers. This PRD attempts to create deterministic rules to: 1) label models with compatibility signals, 2) decide when to pin a model version by default, and 3) define a small set of runtime sanity checks that must pass before a catalog entry goes public.
scope_clarification: In scope: intake metadata contract, deterministic pinning heuristics, runtime compatibility tags, minimal artifact list (model card, provenance, smoke prompts, perf profile), and acceptance-test definitions. Out of scope: full automated verification pipeline (separate eng ticket), long-term eval suite expansion, or billing/price assignment. Rollout for this framework will be limited to new open-model submissions; existing catalog entries will be grandfathered but encouraged to adopt metadata over the next two release cycles.
required_artifacts: Model card (license, source URL, training data provenance summary)
Canonical model weights URL and sha256
Runtime compatibility hints (dtype, expected KV cache layout, recommended context size)
Smoke prompt set (5-10 prompts) and expected output signatures for structure checks
Baseline perf profile (latency P50/P95 at seq len 128/512 on x86/gpu reference)
pinning_policy_summary:
Heuristic rules to pick pin status at intake:
- Auto-pin required if runtime-compatibility=unknown OR custom-ops=true OR memory_profile>reference-allowed
- Soft-pin (recommended) if model introduces new tokenizer/aliases or has nontrivial shape changes; soft-pinned variants can be unpinned after 3 successful rollout cycles
- Do not pin if compatibility signals are clear, reference kernels exist, and smoke perf is within 1.5x of known baseline for the model class.
Pins must record: pinned_to_version, rationale, and rollback plan.
runtime_sanity_tests: Load and forward pass success on reference infra (no fallback to CPU allowed)
KV cache behavior: forward pass with repeated prefix and verify deterministic tokens across 3 seeds
Memory ceiling test: peak memory < catalog_limit_for_family (configurable)
Latency regression: P95 at seq128 within 1.8x of baseline for family; documented if exceeded
Output signature check: structured outputs match declared shape (for models exposing structured tokens)
Quantization smoke: run 8-bit quantized inference (where advertised) and verify token-level stability on smoke prompts
acceptance_criteria: All required artifacts are present in the intake bundle and links validate (sha256 matches)
Runtime sanity tests pass on staging infra; failures are documented and cause auto-pin=true
Compatibility tags assigned (e.g., 'kv-v1','no-custom-ops','quant-ready') and stored in metadata
If auto-pin=true, the catalog entry includes a rollback playbook and a canary rollout plan
Documentation: model card includes clear license and provenance; consumer docs include expected cost/latency deltas
PM sign-off: catalog listing draft reviewed and approved by runtime PM and an infra engineer
Monitoring hooks: minimal telemetry (latency, error-rate, token-cost) are instrumented for the variant
rollout_plan: 1) Gate intake with metadata checklist in the intake form (immediate). 2) For first 30 days, every accepted open-model goes through an 'intake canary' — traffic routed to 0% by default with nightly synthetic smoke runs. 3) If smoke and telemetry for 7 days are green, move to 10% traffic and enable customer-facing listing. 4) After 3 successful 10% windows with no regression, mark as 'catalog-stable' and consider soft-unpin if previously soft-pinned. 5) Any safety or perf regression triggers immediate rollback to previous pinned variant and incident review.
implementation_notes:
- Define a minimal schema for runtime_compatibility hints (flat key-value strings) and expose in catalog API.
- Engineering will own automated runtime sanity harness (ENG ticket TBD) but PM will validate checklist and UX changes for intake flow.
- Add a 'pin rationale' field to catalog entries to make human decisions discoverable.
- Consider a 'compatibility score' later but initial rollout should use deterministic tags, not scores.
metrics_to_track: Number of intake submissions missing required artifacts
Percent of accepted models auto-pinned at intake
Time from submission to public listing (target < 7 days for compliant bundles)
Number of post-listing regressions (runtime/quality) per 100 models
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Overly strict pinning slows catalog growth. Mitigation: soft-pin option with documented path to unpin after 3 green rollouts.
Risk: Missing kernel support causes runtime failures. Mitigation: require explicit compatibility hints and run mandatory KV and forward-pass tests before public listing.
Risk: Too many manual triage escalations. Mitigation: incremental rollout and weekly triage meeting for first month.
